column2: req_desc

Account sign-up
Signing up answers the same accepted response and queues exactly one confirmation-subject mail whether or not the address is already registered, as qualified in Business rules and Services.

Email verification
A confirmation link verifies its account once, and only while it is within the verification lifetime; used, superseded or expired links answer invalid_token.

Sign-in and session
Signing in with the right password starts a session cookie and returns a fresh CSRF token, a wrong password or unknown email gets the identical invalid_credentials answer, and signing out ends the session.

Password reset
A reset request answers identically for any address, the reset link works once and only within the reset lifetime, and completing it ends every existing session of that account.

Sign-in and mail throttles
Sign-in attempts, reset requests and confirmation resends beyond the limits in Business rules answer rate_limited with a Retry-After header, and exactly the limit succeeds even when the requests arrive at the same instant.

One live link per account
When several confirmation or reset links for one account are issued at the same instant, exactly one of each kind works afterwards, the one issued last, and every other answers invalid_token.

Session end on open screens
After sign-out the browser's Back button shows the sign-in screen with the signed-out notice, and a session ended elsewhere answers unauthenticated and shows the session-ended alert on every open screen within the live bound.

Onboarding feedback states
Sign-up, sign-in, resend, forgot, reset and sign-out show their published pending, success, error and field-error copy in the named live regions.

Onboarding journey
A visitor signs up in the browser, confirms through the inbox link, signs in and lands on the starter island with the top rule showing the seeded starter values.

Intent-only building requests
Placing, moving or upgrading a building accepts only the published intent fields, and any extra field such as a level, finish time, cost or owner is rejected with a field error and nothing is stored.

Placement rules
A building is placed only when its rotated footprint lies in the build area, overlaps nothing, stays within its type's count limit and is affordable with a free builder, and each failure answers its published code.

Upgrades and builders
An upgrade needs a free builder, a high enough island saltmark and the level's cost, finishes at a server-computed time, and the free-builder count always equals the saltmark-derived builder total minus active jobs.

Race-safe spends
Concurrent spends on one island never take a balance below zero or use more builders than exist, and each losing request answers insufficient_resources or no_free_builder.

Cancel and move
Cancelling a job before its finish time refunds its cost up to storage room and frees its builder, a cancel at or after the finish time answers job_already_finished while the level is gained, and moving or rotating keeps the level and any running job.

Building feedback states
Place, move and upgrade show their published pending, success, error and field-error copy in the named live regions.

Build journey
In the browser an islander places, rotates and confirms a new building, sees it in the builder queue with a countdown, and sees its level badge and the derived counters update when the job completes.

Producer collection
Collecting a producer credits the output accrued since its last collection, computed from server timestamps and capped by its buffer and storage room, reports any amount lost, and concurrent collects of one producer credit that output exactly once.

Paired resource ledger
Every resource and unit movement is a pair of ledger rows that sum to zero, every balance equals the sum of its rows, and no stored amount ever exceeds its derived storage cap.

Army training and housing
Training charges the published cost, refuses batches that would overflow derived housing, and adds each batch's units to the army at its server-computed finish time.

Training queue order
Training batches run one after another in queue order, and cancelling a waiting or running batch refunds its cost up to storage room and moves every later batch's start and finish as Business rules publish.

Live readouts across tabs
An islander's open screens show the top rule and queues changed by another tab, or by a job or batch finishing on the server, within the live bound and without a reload.

Economy feedback states
Collect, train, cancel job and cancel training show their published pending, success, error and field-error copy in the named live regions.

Economy journey
In the browser an islander collects producers, trains and cancels units and sees the resource, builder and army readouts change to the server's values after each action.

Scout view
A scout report contains only the published fields (layout, levels, lootable amounts and public identity) and never the defender's email, time zone, shield end, army or training queue.

Private villages and raids
Full village, ledger, raid and snapshot reads answer not_found for any island or raid the caller does not own, attack or defend.

Raid eligibility
Scouting or locking your own island, a shielded island, an island already under attack, or a target still in your same-target cooldown answers its published conflict code.

Single raid lock
When several raiders lock the same island at once, exactly one receives the raid and every other gets already_under_attack.

Deploy validation
Deploy batches accept only units reserved at lock, cells on the tidal ring, and non-decreasing ticks inside the raid window, and they answer field errors keyed by deploy position.

Idempotent raid requests
Start-raid, deploy and finalize requests return their stored response when an Idempotency-Key is repeated, and answer idempotency_key_reused when the same key comes with a different body.

Raid start feedback states
Next island, start raid and deploy show their published pending, success and error copy in the named live regions.

Raid journey
In the browser a verified raider scouts a match, starts the raid, deploys units on the tidal ring during the raid clock, ends the raid and sees the server's result.

Finalize deadline
A raid not finalized before its finalize deadline ends abandoned with the deadline end reason: it moves no units, loot or trophies, grants no shield, and releases its lock.

Deterministic battle
Resolving a raid runs the published simulation on the stored seed, layout, deploy list and resolution lootable amounts, so the same inputs always produce the same per-tick hashes, destruction, stars and loot.

Loot at resolution
A resolved raid takes its lootable amounts from the defender's balances at the moment resolution commits, after any defender spend that committed first, and moves each looted resource as a defender debit and an equal raider credit capped by the raider's storage room.

Trophies, leagues and star bonus
A resolved raid changes both players' trophies by the published amounts without going below zero, places each player in the league their trophies fall in, and grants the star bonus only within the attacker's daily cap for their local day.

Shield and cooldown
A defence that concedes two or more stars shields the defender for exactly the shield lifetime from resolution, no raid lock commits on that island while the shield runs, and every resolved raid starts the attacker's same-target cooldown for exactly the cooldown lifetime.

Defender's open screen
The defender's open village shows the under-attack notice within the live bound of a lock and, within the same bound of resolution, the post-raid readouts, the shield end and the new Raid log row.

Raid result feedback states
End raid and the Raid log show their published pending, success and error copy in the named live regions.

Raid log journey
In the browser a defender finds the raid against them in the Raid log with its result and opens its replay from there.

Raid snapshots
The snapshot endpoint returns to a participant, for any tick of a resolved raid, that tick's destruction, stars, loot, building and unit state and the published state hash, and the final tick equals the raid's result.

Wake dial scrubbing
Dragging around the Wake dial moves one tick per degree, redraws the scene at every notch crossed as its drawn-tick attribute shows, and on every settle sets the scene's tick, destruction, stars, loot and hash attributes to that tick's snapshot.

Dial coast and settle
Releasing the dial after a fling makes it coast with the published friction and then spring-settle on a whole tick within the raid's range, never resting between ticks.

Dial keyboard and reduced motion
Arrow, Page Up, Page Down, Home and End keys step the dial, and with reduced motion the dial becomes a stepped slider with tick buttons and a numeric input that cut straight to each snapshot.

Replay feedback states
Opening a replay shows the published loading, ready and error copy in the named live regions.

Replay journey
In the browser a participant opens a replay, scrubs forward and back and sees buildings fall at their recorded ticks while the inner numerals match the server.

Daily chest and streak
The daily chest can be claimed once per local day in the islander's saved time zone, pays the step of the 7-step streak table the claim reaches, and of several claims at the same instant exactly one succeeds.

Weekly tide-league bonus
The league bonus can be claimed once per local week starting Monday at local midnight in the islander's saved zone, correct across daylight-saving weeks and month and year boundaries, and pays the bonus of the islander's current league.

Time-zone change and reward clocks
After the islander changes their saved time zone, the next daily chest and league bonus open at the instants Business rules publish, so no change of zone ever yields an extra claim.

Rewards feedback states
Opening the chest and claiming the league bonus show their published copy, and an open Rewards panel updates its next-unlock texts within the live bound after a time-zone change.

Rewards journey
In the browser an islander opens the daily chest and claims the league bonus, sees the credited amounts in the top rule, and then sees the next chest and next league bonus times in their own local time.

Clan founding and invitations
A verified islander founds a clan as its skipper, wardens invite by email with an identical answer for any address and exactly one invitation mail per request, and an invitee joins only while the clan has room and the invitation is still valid.

Warden powers
Promote, demote, remove-member and delete-message follow the published role rules, and a lower role calling them directly answers forbidden.

Immediate role changes
A demotion or removal takes effect on the affected member's very next request in the same session, and concurrent role changes on one member apply one at a time as Business rules publish.

Skipper succession
When the skipper leaves, the skipper role passes to the member Business rules name, and a clan whose last member leaves is dissolved and frees its name at once.

Clan chat
Members post plain-text messages that every clanmate sees exactly as typed, and a warden's deletion replaces the message for everyone with the removal notice.

Clan chat throttle
Clan chat posts beyond the published limit answer rate_limited with a Retry-After header, and exactly the limit is stored even when posts arrive at the same instant.

Clan screens stay live
New and deleted messages and a member's removal show on every affected open Clan panel within the live bound, and the Clan link counts unread messages while the chat log is hidden.

Clan league standing
The league table ranks clans by the summed trophies of their current members, and the clan view shows its own rank.

Clan feedback states
Founding, inviting, accepting, promoting, demoting, removing, leaving, posting and deleting show their published pending, success, error and field-error copy in the named live regions.

Clan journey
In the browser a skipper founds a clan, invites by email, sees the invitee join, promotes them to mate and demotes them, and moderates chat.

Donation requests
A member keeps at most one open request naming a unit and count and may cancel it, clanmates donate up to what it still needs and at most three each, and a donation that commits after the request closed or after the recipient's housing filled is refused with its published code.

Donor daily cap
Each donor gives at most 8 units per local day in their own saved time zone, and a donation beyond that answers donation_cap_reached with the next allowed instant.

Paired donations and counters
Every donation writes a donor debit and an equal recipient credit of units, and each member's donated, received and housing counters equal what the records show.

Donation progress on open screens
The requester's open Clan panel shows each donation's progress on their request within the live bound.

Donation feedback states
Requesting, donating and cancelling a request show their published pending, success, error and field-error copy in the named live regions.

Donation journey
In the browser a member posts a request, a clanmate donates, and both see the request fill and their armies and counters change.

Operator raid re-run
The studio operator re-runs any resolved raid from its stored inputs and sees whether every tick's hash matches, while anyone else calling operator routes gets forbidden.

Database outage and recovery
With PostgreSQL unreachable the app keeps answering its health check and answers database_unavailable elsewhere, leaves only whole ledger pairs, abandons raids whose deadline passed meanwhile, and serves normally again once the database returns, with no restart.

Mail outage queue
Mail requested while Mailpit is unreachable is queued and delivered exactly once after Mailpit returns, while the request still gets its normal answer.

Opaque errors
Every error body uses the one published shape and never contains a stack trace, SQL text, file path, library name or secret.

Malformed ids
Every route with an id in its path answers not_found for ids that are zero, negative, beyond the published maximum, not plain decimal digits or shaped like a UUID, and never answers 500 for them.

Operations feedback states
Re-running a raid and checking the ledger show their published pending, success and error copy in the named live regions.

Operator journey
In the browser the operator signs in, reads the service status, re-runs a disputed raid by ID and checks the ledger.

Keyboard building placement
An islander can select, place, rotate, move and confirm a building, and open and close the Build dialog, using only the keyboard.

Touch camera and reduced motion
On a touch screen one finger pans, a pinch zooms and a two-finger twist rotates the island, and with reduced motion build, upgrade and raid animations become instant state changes.

Grid feedback states
Keyboard cursor moves and ghost confirmations announce their published copy, and confirming an invalid ghost sends no request and shows the invalid-spot copy.

Run manifest and health
The app installs, builds and serves from the run manifest on the published port, and its health path answers the published body.

Session and request boundary
State changes need the session cookie plus a matching CSRF token from the same origin, bodies over the size limit or of the wrong type are refused, and only built client files are served.

Responsive layout
Island screens at tablet and laptop sizes keep the published centre box clear of interface, and every screen at phone, tablet and laptop sizes has no horizontal overflow and tap targets of at least 44 pixels.

Flat-plan fallback
Without WebGL the island shows as a flat top-down plan with the same controls, data attributes and replay behaviour.

Visual identity
Every screen uses the dusky indigo, salt-white and single kiln-orange identity with the published typefaces, flat rule-separated panels and a procedural 3D island.

Shared simulation module
The battle rules exist once in the source and are imported by both the server's resolution and the browser's replay and preview.

Configuration from environment
Every service address, credential, lifetime and port is read from the published environment variables at start, and none is hard-coded or sent to the browser.

Profile feedback states
Saving the profile shows its published pending, success, error and field-error copy in the named live regions.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve commands and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and nothing else is needed to install, build and serve.
/app/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree as reported by npm ls --omit=dev --all --json), every bundled font and the icon set, each with its licence.
Shipped packages (that same production dependency tree) and bundled assets use only the MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1 licences.
PostgreSQL is the only datastore: no SQLite, Redis, document stores or state files; everything that must outlive a restart lives in PostgreSQL.
Application source is TypeScript; no hand-written JavaScript source files exist outside generated build output and tool configuration.
The browser loads nothing from other origins; fonts, icons, scripts and styles are bundled and served by the app.
package-lock.json is committed, and install uses it.
The provided service compose files and their seeded credentials are left unchanged.
